summary: Iter85 batch review: (1) Attendance phase 2 split (routes/attendance_actions.py), (2) grams_per_unit unit-conversions on PATCH /api/meals/items + conversion object in POST /api/meals/issues/suggest, (3) default headcount prefill (muster | prev_day | manual). Caught & FIXED a critical bug introduced by phase 2: both `/api/attendance/recalc-late` and `/api/attendance/resolve-stale` returned 422 (body treated as query param) because their Pydantic request models (RecalcLateIn, ResolveStaleIn) were defined inside make_router() while the module uses `from __future__ import annotations` — FastAPI's forward-ref resolution falls back to module globals and could not find the local classes. Fix: moved both classes to module scope alongside GeoToggleIn/TempExitIn/etc. After fix, 20/20 iter85 tests pass; combined with iter83+iter84 regression suites and test_early_out_helper the full battery is 114/114 PASS. Frontend Suggest dialog verified: issues-suggest-btn opens, date=2026-10-02 shows subtitle 'Fri, 02 Oct 2026 · Friday menu', 5x suggest-headcount-src-<meal> testids with 'yesterday: N' labels (Breakfast 13, Lunch 21 matching spec), suggest-conversions box present with 2 conv-notes/inputs/saves (Oil at 1 L = [1000 placeholder] g with 'assumed 1 g ≈ 1 ml', plus Banana), Save disabled when empty and enabled after typing positive number. Self Check-in page (/) renders Check-In card + 'I showed up' button + 'Forgot to punch in earlier?' correction link. No DB writes to real data — all throwaway resources (ZZ Test staff + attendance/temp_exits/audit rows + ZZ Test Oil item) were deleted during fixture teardown.

critical.issue: Phase 2 split regression — RecalcLateIn/ResolveStaleIn were declared inside make_router(); with `from __future__ import annotations` FastAPI could not resolve the forward refs so the `body` param was treated as a query parameter → every call returned 422 {loc:[query,body], msg:Field required}. FIXED in this run by promoting both models to module scope.

Main agent should pull in the moved Pydantic class definitions (RecalcLateIn, ResolveStaleIn) in future phases of the split to avoid the same pitfall when stacking `from __future__ import annotations` with locally-scoped BaseModel request bodies.

rca of the issue: RCA: Phase 2 attendance split moved classes GeoToggleIn/MarkMemberIn/ScanCardIn/TempExitIn/TempReturnIn to module scope at the top of routes/attendance_actions.py, but RecalcLateIn and ResolveStaleIn were authored INSIDE the make_router() factory. The module declares `from __future__ import annotations`, which turns every type annotation into a string. FastAPI resolves those strings via `typing.get_type_hints()`, which can only see the module's global namespace — not local variables of enclosing functions. When resolution fails, FastAPI treats the parameter as a query/body-form primitive rather than a Pydantic model, producing 422 'Field required' for the parameter name itself. Reproduction: `curl -X POST /api/attendance/recalc-late -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"start":"2026-10-01","end":"2026-10-01"}'` → 422. Mitigation: moved the two offending classes to module scope. Prevention: lint/enforce that all BaseModel request-body classes live at module level when PEP-563 is active.
